t.5.17.1: Then, at that very time, the blameless princess saw him, endowed with beauty and youth and adorned with the finest ornaments.
t.5.17.2: Then, at the very sight of Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, the fair-hipped Vaidehī trembled like a plantain tree in a gust of wind.
t.5.17.3: Covering her belly with her thighs and her breasts with her arms, the large-eyed lady of lovely complexion sat there, weeping.
t.5.17.4: Daśagrīva, however, saw Vaidehī, guarded by hosts of rākṣasīs, wretched and stricken with sorrow, like a ship sinking in the ocean.
t.5.17.5: Her, seated on the bare ground, rigid in her vows, like a branch of a great tree severed and fallen to the earth, her limbs smeared with dirt as her only ornament, she who was worthy of adornment yet went unadorned.
t.5.17.6: She seemed to be journeying to the side of Rāma, the lion among kings, whose self was known, borne on the chariots of her heart's desires yoked with the horses of resolve.
t.5.17.7: She was withering away and weeping, alone, wholly given over to brooding and grief, seeing no end to her sorrow: that lovely woman devoted to Rāma.
t.5.17.8: Writhing and overpowered, she was like the consort of a lord of serpents, like Rohiṇī smothered in smoke by the planet Dhūmaketu.
t.5.17.10: She was like great glory fallen into ruin, like faith that has been scorned, like wisdom wasted away, like hope that has been shattered.
t.5.17.9: He saw her, born into a righteous family of good conduct and character, devoted to proper custom, yet looking as though she had undergone a second rite of birth and been born again into a lowly family.
t.5.17.11: She was like a hope for the future that had been shattered, like a command that had been defied, like a quarter of the sky ablaze at the hour of doom, like worship whose offering had been snatched away.
t.5.17.12: He saw her like a ravaged lotus pond, like an army whose heroes have been slain, like radiance worn away by austerity, like a river dwindled almost dry.
t.5.17.13: She was like a sacrificial altar that has been defiled, like a tongue of fire that has died down, like a full-moon night whose lunar disc has been swallowed by Rāhu.
t.5.17.15: Afflicted with grief for her husband and withered, she was like a river whose waters have been drained away; bereft of all adornment and grooming, she was like a night in the dark fortnight.
t.5.17.14: She was like a lotus pond thrown into turmoil, its leaves and lotuses torn up, its birds scattered in terror, ravaged by the trunk of an elephant.
t.5.17.16: She was delicate and lovely of limb, fit to dwell in an inner chamber studded with jewels, yet she seemed scorched by the heat, like a lotus stalk freshly pulled from the water.
t.5.17.17: She was like the mate of a lordly elephant, captured and tied to a post, parted from the leader of her herd, sighing and sorely stricken with grief.
t.5.17.18: Effortlessly beautiful with her single long braid, she shone like the earth adorned with a dark line of forest when the clouds have departed.
t.5.17.19: Worn away by fasting, by grief, by brooding and by fear, she was emaciated and wretched, eating but little, one whose only wealth was her austerity.
t.5.17.20: He beheld her, stricken with sorrow, her palms joined like a goddess, praying with her heart devoted to the foremost of the Raghus for the defeat of Daśagrīva.
t.5.17.21: Rāvaṇa, to his own destruction, tried to seduce the blameless Maithilī, who was looking about and weeping, whose long eyes were white, tinged with copper and fringed with lovely lashes, and who was utterly devoted to Rāma.
